page: Microsoft Azure F8-4amds_v7 is a memory-intensive virtual machine belonging to the Famdsv7 server family. It is built on the x86_64 architecture and runs on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The server features 4 dedicated physical cores and 4 vCPUs powered by an AMD EPYC 9V45 processor operating at a clock speed of 4.5 GHz. It is equipped with 64.0 GB of system memory, providing a high resource density of 16.0 GB of RAM per core. For local storage, the instance includes a bundled 945 GB NVMe SSD, and it is capable of utilizing Premium Storage. No GPUs are included in this configuration.

Benchmark data highlights strong single-core performance, with stress-ng single-core CPU performance, single-threaded gzip compression, and single-threaded bzip3 decompression all ranking in the top tier. However, multi-core performance scales to average levels, as shown by stress-ng multi-core CPU performance, PassMark CPU scores, and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression falling into the middle tier. Memory bandwidth tests for both read and write operations also register in the average tier. For lightweight AI workloads, the server demonstrates strong text generation speeds with a small 135M LLM model, though prompt processing for medium 7B models is weak, representing a clear tradeoff for larger model inference.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the F8-4amds_v7 offers a high memory-to-vCPU ratio alongside fast single-core processing and local NVMe storage, making it a resource-dense option for workloads that do not require massive parallelization. The combination of high-speed AMD EPYC cores, 64.0 GB of RAM, and fast local NVMe SSD storage makes this server well-suited for memory-intensive applications, database operations, caching layers like Redis, and single-threaded data processing tasks.
